text:
maya: Heads-up — getting repeated kv-cache burn alerts for tenant t-42 this morning. Error budget dropped quickly around 07:10 UTC. Anyone know the quickest place to pull logs/traces/dashboards for triage?

jon: Start with the Grafana panel `kv-cache / tenant-latency` -> https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abc123/kv-cache?orgId=1&var-tenant=t-42 . 95p latency spikes at ~07:12 UTC line up with the alert.

alex: Raw logs live in Loki (pushgateway -> loki). Quick LogQL to filter for relevant errors: 
```
{app="kv-cache"} |= "t-42" |~ "timeout|evict|OOM|error"
```
Run for the 07:00-07:30 UTC range.

carla: For traces, open the Grafana panel and click the trace link (Tempo/Jaeger). If you want to search directly: service=kv-cache, tag tenant_id=t-42 in Tempo's trace search. The trace will show KV miss/hotspot propagation.

sam: Also check Prometheus: `kv_cache_hit_ratio{tenant="t-42"}` and `kv_cache_total_requests`. If hit ratio drops, token generation increases and you'll see burn.

maya: Quick question — alert currently uses a 5m burn window and threshold 1.5x baseline. Seems noisy when tenants get transient throttles. Should we widen the window?

jon: The rule is in infra/alerts/kv_cache.rules.yml. Expr uses `increase(kv_cache_burn[5m]) > 1.5 * baseline`. We could change to 15m or add `for: 10m` to reduce flapping. I'll open a PR to propose `for: 10m` + keep threshold.

alex: If it's tenant-scoped noise we can also add an exclusion for known test tenants or noisy customers using `label_replace` or by scoping alerts to tenants with SLA tags. Alternatively add a small smoothing function.

sre-bot: incident 0x4f3a created: kv-cache-burn-t-42 — https://incidents.internal/0x4f3a

carla: Runbook link: https://docs.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-burn.md — follow steps: 1) identify tenant, 2) grab top traces, 3) check host OOM/CPU, 4) escalate if needed.

maya: I'll pull logs/traces now and paste the interesting snippets. If we change the alert, please @carla for review on the PR. :thumbsup: 

sam: Note — node-exporter alerted minor OOM on host gpu-04 at 07:10 (see prometheus alert node_oom_gpu_04). Could be correlated.

jon: Cool — I'll create a dashboard snapshot and raise the PR to set `for: 10m` and add a tenant-exclusion example. pinging @carla for review. :eyes:
